scope: Named honeyberry / haskap (Lonicera caerulea) cultivars, shippable to Annandale, NJ (zone 6b/7a). Nearly all need a second variety that blooms at the same time, so each variety is tagged early or late bloomer where sellers agree. In zone 6–7, late bloomers (the Boreal series and the Japanese types from Maxine Thompson) usually do better; early bloomers like Tundra and Indigo Gem can open too soon and get caught by late freezes. Names overlap: Berry Blue = Czech #17 = Berry Smart Blue; Yezberry Solo = Kapu; Yezberry Maxie = Kuchi.

varieties.name: Aurora
varieties.summary: Very large, firm, sweet-tasting berries; a favorite for fresh eating.
varieties.description: University of Saskatchewan release with some of the largest berries (about 2.7 g), firm with a dry scar, and a low-acid balance that tastes sweet. Upright 5–6' bush, mildew resistant. Blooms early but ripens late; in zone 6 and warmer it can break dormancy too early at some sites. Pair with Honey Bee, Indigo Gem or Boreal Beast.

varieties.name: Honey Bee
varieties.summary: Large berries with a light tartness; very productive, holds fruit until fully ripe.
varieties.description: University of Saskatchewan release. Large berries (about 1.9 g) on an upright 5–6' bush; holds fruit firmly until ripe, then detaches easily. Very productive (about 9 lb at five years). Leaves resist sunburn, wind and mildew. A standard pollinizer for Aurora.

varieties.name: Boreal Blizzard
varieties.summary: Largest berries of the Saskatchewan line, with outstanding tang.
varieties.description: University of Saskatchewan (2016), 50% Japanese and 50% Russian. Very large “surfboard” berries (2.8 g average) with excellent flavor; softer than Aurora. Upright 5'+ bush, excellent mildew and sunscald resistance. Late-blooming category; pollinize with Boreal Beast or Honey Bee.

varieties.name: Boreal Beast
varieties.summary: Excellent aroma and flavor; fruit holds on the bush for weeks.
varieties.description: University of Saskatchewan (2016), half Japanese with Russian and Kuril ancestry. Thick heart-shaped berries with an excellent aroma; one Wyoming grower reports fruit holding up to three weeks after coloring and Brix above 20. Late-blooming; pairs with Blizzard and Beauty, and with Aurora in some climates.

varieties.name: Boreal Beauty
varieties.summary: Heavy crops of large, firm heart-shaped berries; latest Saskatchewan bloomer.
varieties.description: University of Saskatchewan (2016). Large firm berries (2.6 g average) with a blueberry-like texture, heavy yields, excellent mildew resistance. The latest-blooming Saskatchewan variety, overlapping the Japanese types (Solo, Maxie, Keiko). Drops fruit more readily than Blizzard or Beast.

varieties.name: Borealis
varieties.summary: Compact Saskatchewan variety with large, sweet berries.
varieties.description: University of Saskatchewan release with large, sweet berries on a compact, dense bush. Some growers find the dense leaf canopy makes picking harder.

varieties.name: Indigo Gem
varieties.summary: Sweet, slightly chewy berries; one of the first to ripen.
varieties.description: University of Saskatchewan release. Early blooming and ripening, medium berries (1.3 g) prized for fresh eating, higher yield than Tundra and good for wine. Needs a non-Indigo, non-Tundra pollinizer such as Aurora or Berry Blue.

varieties.name: Tundra
varieties.summary: Very firm berries with a long shelf life; easy picking.
varieties.description: University of Saskatchewan release. Firm, melt-in-the-mouth berries (1.5 g) with a long shelf life, excellent for wine. Early blooming and best suited to zones 2–4; growers in zone 7 report early bloomers like Tundra getting caught by late freezes.

varieties.name: Berry Blue
varieties.summary: Big, fast-growing bush with tart tube-shaped berries; a classic pollinizer.
varieties.description: Czech selection #17, sold as Berry Blue™ or Berry Smart Blue. Fast-growing, 6–10' bush with medium tube-shaped berries that are tart until fully ripe. Long early bloom makes it a common pollinizer for Aurora and the Indigo series. Leaves sunburn easily but fruiting isn't affected.

varieties.name: Blue Banana
varieties.summary: Large, elongated sweet berries; high yield.
varieties.description: Russian-type variety bred by Lidia Delafield Stuart of Berries Unlimited. Large, elongated sweet berries good fresh or processed, estimated 6–12 lb per plant. Early-to-mid bloom (One Green World lists it as late); can drop berries in wind.

varieties.name: Strawberry Sensation
varieties.summary: Pure Japanese late bloomer with a strawberry aftertaste; very heavy cropper.
varieties.description: 100% Japanese genetics, bred by Lidia Delafield Stuart of Berries Unlimited. Thick oval, firm berries with a strawberry aftertaste; one commercial grower calls it near the top of his collection for flavor. Late bloomer; pair with Giant's Heart or other late types.

varieties.name: Giant's Heart
varieties.summary: Large heart-shaped berries, sweeter than most, with a smoky plum finish.
varieties.description: 100% Japanese genetics, bred by Lidia Delafield Stuart of Berries Unlimited. Large, firm heart-shaped berries that detach easily; sweeter than most with a smoked-plum aftertaste. Late bloomer.

varieties.name: Yezberry Solo
varieties.summary: The only verified self-fertile honeyberry; pure Japanese late bloomer.
varieties.description: Japanese haskap ‘Kapu’ from Dr. Maxine Thompson's Oregon breeding program, sold as Yezberry® Solo™. The one variety growers verify as self-pollinating, though a partner still raises yields. Milder, less tangy berries than Russian types; late blooming, suited to temperate climates.

varieties.name: Yezberry Maxie
varieties.summary: Pure Japanese late bloomer from Maxine Thompson; partner for Solo.
varieties.description: Japanese haskap ‘Kuchi’ from Dr. Maxine Thompson's program, sold as Yezberry® Maxie™. Late-blooming, milder flavor than Russian types; the usual partner for Solo.

varieties.name: Keiko
varieties.summary: One of the sweetest; medium-large oval berries, excellent for wine.
varieties.description: Japanese haskap from Dr. Maxine Thompson's program. Medium-large oval berries with a flattened tip, tart-sweet and among the sweetest (Brix about 13.5), rated excellent for wine. Late bloomer; 5–6' bush. Somewhat prone to powdery mildew.

varieties.name: Tana
varieties.summary: Firm, tart-sweet Japanese berries that hold on the bush.
varieties.description: Japanese haskap from Dr. Maxine Thompson's program. Medium-large, firm, tart-sweet berries with a rounded tip; one grower reports fruit holding three weeks on the bush. Late bloomer.

varieties.name: Willa
varieties.summary: Mild, sweet-tasting Japanese berries; first of the late types to ripen.
varieties.description: Japanese haskap from Dr. Maxine Thompson's program. Oval-round berries with a mild taste many call sweet (Brix 15); one of the first late-blooming varieties to flower and ripen. Softer, and drops more in strong wind.

varieties.name: Blue Moose
varieties.summary: Sweet Russian-type variety; heavy bearer.
varieties.description: Russian-type honeyberry sold by Stark Bro's and others; rated sweet in Berries Unlimited's trials.

varieties.name: Blue Diamond
varieties.summary: Large dark berries; tart-sweet Russian type.
varieties.description: Russian-type honeyberry with large, dark berries and a tart-sweet flavor.

varieties.name: Blue Palm
varieties.summary: Tart-sweet Russian type blooming about a week after the earliest.
varieties.description: Russian-type honeyberry; tart-sweet berries, blooming about a week after the earliest varieties.

varieties.name: Happy Giant
varieties.summary: Large purple-blue elongated berries, sweeter than most.
varieties.description: Russian-type honeyberry with large, purply-blue elongated berries. Stark Bro's suggests Borealis, Blue Diamond, Blue Moose or Blue Palm as pollinizers.

varieties.name: Blue Moon
varieties.summary: Late-blooming, low mounding shrub with soft velvety leaves.
varieties.description: Late-blooming variety forming a low, mounding shrub.

varieties.name: Blue Velvet
varieties.summary: Late bloomer with unusual grey-green velvety leaves.
varieties.description: Late-blooming cultivar growing 3–4' tall and wide, with unusual grey-green, velvety leaves.

varieties.name: Blue Mist
varieties.summary: Hardy Japanese import, late blooming, larger-than-average berries.
varieties.description: Exceptionally hardy Japanese import; late blooming with abundant crops of larger-than-average berries.

varieties.name: Blue Pacific
varieties.summary: Russian Far East variety with a compact spreading form.
varieties.description: From the east coast of Russia; compact, spreading form with light green foliage.

varieties.name: Blue Sea
varieties.summary: Low spreading bush with large, sweet berries.
varieties.description: Chosen for generous crops of large, sweet berries on a low, spreading bush.

varieties.name: Blue Hokkaido
varieties.summary: Late bloomer recommended where spring weather swings.
varieties.description: Late-blooming honeyberry recommended for growers with variable spring weather.

varieties.name: Blue Pagoda
varieties.summary: Hardy Japanese import with teardrop-shaped fruit.
varieties.description: Exceptionally hardy Japanese import; late blooming, with an unusual teardrop fruit shape.

varieties.name: Blue Belle
varieties.summary: Early bloomer with large, oval deep-blue berries on a 5–6' bush.
varieties.description: Sold as Blue Belle (‘Berry Smart Belle’). Early blooming, with good crops of large, oval, deep blue berries on a 5–6' bush.

varieties.name: Blue Bird
varieties.summary: Reliably productive early bloomer with light blue fruit.
varieties.description: Early-blooming, reliably productive variety with light blue fruit ripening in May in the Pacific Northwest.

varieties.name: Blue Horn
varieties.summary: Early-blooming tart-sweet variety.
varieties.description: Early-blooming Russian-type honeyberry with tart-sweet berries.

varieties.name: Blue Treasure
varieties.summary: Late Japanese-type variety from Berries Unlimited.
varieties.description: Late-ripening variety from Berries Unlimited, sold as tissue-cultured plants.

varieties.name: Honey Glen
varieties.summary: Early-mid season Berries Unlimited cultivar (patent pending).
varieties.description: New early-to-mid season cultivar from Berries Unlimited.

varieties.name: Blue Delight
varieties.summary: Berries Unlimited variety.
varieties.description: Variety sold by Berries Unlimited, which says to buy from them to be sure of the true variety.

varieties.name: Blue Typhoon
varieties.summary: Late-season Japanese-type honeyberry from Berries Unlimited with sweet, fluffy, cylindrical berries.
varieties.description: A Japanese-heritage Lonicera caerulea selection sold exclusively by Berries Unlimited under US trademark (plant patent pending through 2038). Berries are medium-large, very sweet and shaped like a short, fluffy cylinder; the tissue-cultured plant is a late bloomer hardy to zone 2 and needs a compatible late-season partner such as Giant's Heart or Blue Treasure.

varieties.name: Blue Stuart
varieties.summary: Russian-type honeyberry in the Blue Perfection group, valued for its very sweet, almost round berries.
varieties.description: A Russian-heritage Lonicera caerulea selection in the Blue Perfection family, sold by Berries Unlimited under US trademark (plant patent pending through 2038). The medium-large, nearly round berries are described as very sweet with a distinctive flavor; the tissue-cultured plant blooms early-to-mid season and is hardy to zone 2.

varieties.name: Yezberry Honey Bunch
varieties.summary: Compact Japanese-type haskap in the Yezberry series, with large sweet berries on a half-sized plant.
varieties.description: Part of the Yezberry series of pure Japanese Lonicera caerulea selections (US plant patent 28,662), distinct from Russian-heritage types like the Sugar Mountain series. The mounded shrub stays compact at 3-5 feet, about half the size of other honeyberries, with large, plump, sweet berries that ripen in early summer; it blooms a bit later than earlier types, which helps it dodge spring frosts.
notes: No longer listed by Proven Winners; still sold by Park Seed as of Oct 2026.

varieties.name: Boreal Bliss
varieties.summary: New University of Saskatchewan haskap, late-blooming, with wild Canadian parentage.
varieties.description: Released by the University of Saskatchewan fruit breeding program from a 2011 cross of a Maxine Thompson Japanese selection with wild Canadian haskap pollen from Nova Scotia, making it the first released haskap cultivar with wild Canadian lineage. Fruit is arrowhead-shaped, firm and flavorful (Brix ~21.5). The bush is upright with strong vigor and good mildew resistance, blooming the third week of May and ripening in late July in Saskatoon, timed to cross-pollinate with Boreal Beast.
notes: Just releasing; listed as waitlist/2026 release by multiple sellers.

varieties.name: Indigo Treat
varieties.summary: Compact Lonicera caerulea cultivar with elongated dark blue berries.
varieties.description: A Lonicera caerulea cultivar grown for its elongated, dark blue, firm and juicy berries with a sweet flavor and slight acidity, good fresh or processed. The shrub is compact and upright with a dense habit well suited to a fruit hedge, reaching about 5 feet tall and wide, with frost-resistant spring flowers and early-summer fruit.

varieties.name: Chito
varieties.summary: Patented Japanese-type haskap bred by Maxine Thompson in Oregon.
varieties.description: Bred by Dr. Maxine Thompson in Corvallis, Oregon and selected in 2004 from her Japanese haskap breeding program (U.S. Plant Patent PP28663). Berries are large and light blue, oval in shape, averaging about 2g with a tart-sweet flavor. The shrub has a slightly open, upright habit to about 2m and is a consistently heavy producer, ripening in mid-June in Oregon.

varieties.name: Taka
varieties.summary: Patented Japanese-type haskap bred by Maxine Thompson in Oregon.
varieties.description: Developed by Dr. Maxine Thompson in Oregon (U.S. Plant Patent PP26707). Produces cylindrical, medium-large berries with a milder, sweeter flavor than many other cultivars, on a moderately vigorous, spreading shrub. Blooms mid-season (mid-May to early June) and is a good pollination match for Chito and other mid-season varieties.

varieties.name: Kawai
varieties.summary: Patented Japanese-type haskap bred by Maxine Thompson in Oregon.
varieties.description: Selected by Dr. Maxine Thompson in Corvallis, Oregon in 2009 from her Japanese haskap breeding program begun in 2000 (U.S. Plant Patent PP28664). Berries are medium-sized, ovate-rectangular with a sweet-tart flavor, averaging about 1.7g. The shrub is vigorous, upright and spreading, with an early-mid-season harvest around early June in Oregon.

varieties.name: Pirika
varieties.summary: Patented Japanese-type haskap bred by Maxine Thompson in Oregon.
varieties.description: Selected by Dr. Maxine Thompson in Corvallis, Oregon in 2008 from a breeding program using Hokkaido, Japan seed stock (U.S. Plant Patent PP28954). Berries are large and elliptical, sweet (Brix ~14), averaging about 2.2g. The shrub is vigorous, upright and spreading with above-average yields, ripening in early-to-mid June in Oregon.

varieties.name: Blue Forest
varieties.summary: Late-blooming honeyberry with large, sweet-tart dark blue fruit.
varieties.description: A late-blooming honeyberry selection offered by One Green World, producing large, dark-blue fruit with a sweet-tart flavor and yields of roughly 5-10 lbs per mature plant. The shrub is compact and spreading, reaching about 2-3 feet tall. It flowers in March, about two months after early-blooming types, and ripens by June; it needs another late-blooming variety nearby for good pollination.

varieties.name: Cinderella
varieties.summary: Early-blooming honeyberry with round, sweet bluish-purple fruit.
varieties.description: A honeyberry cultivar carried by independent garden centers, grown for its round, bluish-purple berries with a sweet flavor suited to fresh eating and preserves. The shrub is a dense, multi-stemmed, rounded form reaching about 3 feet tall and wide. It opens creamy white flowers in early spring and ripens from late spring into early summer; growers note it sets a heavier crop with a second variety planted nearby.

varieties.name: Blue Sky
varieties.summary: Very early-ripening honeyberry from a Siberian breeding line.
varieties.description: An early-blooming honeyberry selection from an amateur breeding program in Siberia, offered by One Green World for its sweet, blueberry-like fruit suited to fresh eating, juice, and preserves. The compact shrub grows 3-4 feet tall, blooms March-April, and ripens in May-June, often about two weeks ahead of strawberries.

varieties.name: Sunrise
varieties.summary: Early-ripening honeyberry sold exclusively through Gurney's, bred as selection '51-02'.
varieties.description: Sunrise (trademarked, breeding code 'Lonicera edulis 51-02') is sold only through Gurney's Seed & Nursery and its Home Depot storefront. Gurney's markets it as an early-ripening, sweet-tart honeyberry and recommends Early Blue as a pollinator partner.

varieties.name: Early Blue
varieties.summary: Early-ripening honeyberry sold exclusively through Gurney's, bred as selection '29-55'.
varieties.description: Early Blue (trademarked, breeding code 'Lonicera edulis 29-55') is sold only through Gurney's Seed & Nursery and its Home Depot storefront. The listing describes early, sweet-tart fruit and pest/leaf-burn resistance, and names Sunrise as its pollinator partner.

varieties.name: Maxine's Opus
varieties.summary: Large, sweet-tart mid-season honeyberry bred by Maxine Thompson's Oregon program; needs a pollinator like Kawai.
varieties.description: Maxine's Opus came out of Maxine Thompson's honeyberry breeding program in Corvallis, Oregon, selected in 2012 from a cross of seedlings '84-105' and '65-18'. It forms a wide, vigorous, spreading bush bearing large, firm, jar-shaped, mid-season fruit with a sweet-tart flavor (about 15 Brix); sellers recommend Kawai as a pollinator partner.

varieties.name: Smokey Blue
varieties.summary: Large, sweet powder-blue berries on a compact spreading bush; an early bloomer.
varieties.description: One Green World describes Smokey Blue as a vigorous, spreading small shrub 2-4 ft tall with large, sweet, high-sugar berries named for their powder-blue skin. It blooms March-April and ripens May-June, so it needs another early bloomer as a partner.

varieties.name: Indigo Yum
varieties.summary: Sweet, early-ripening honeyberry hardy to zone 3.
varieties.description: One Green World lists Indigo Yum as a hardy, early-ripening cultivar with sweet berries for fresh eating, preserves or juice. The bush reaches 3-4 ft, bears 1-2 years after planting, blooms March-April and ripens May-June; it needs a partner with similar bloom time.

varieties.name: Blue Lightning
varieties.summary: Dark blue, sweet-tart honeyberry from the Russian Far East; an early bloomer.
varieties.description: One Green World lists Blue Lightning as a Russian Far East selection with dark blue, sweet-tart berries on an upright bush 4-5 ft tall. It blooms March-April and ripens May-June, so it needs another early bloomer as a partner.

varieties.name: Honey Beast
varieties.summary: Very large, dark blue, very sweet berries from an American-Russian hybrid cultivar.
varieties.description: Sold by Berries Unlimited as an American-Russian hybrid cultivar (PPAF) rated for USDA zones 2-7. Fruit is very large, dark blue and elongated, described as very sweet with a complex flavor. Ripens early to mid season; bloom time and mature size are not stated.

varieties.name: Honey Joy
varieties.summary: Large, oval, very sweet dark blue berries for fresh eating and freezing.
varieties.description: Sold by Berries Unlimited as an American-Russian hybrid (PPAF) rated for USDA zones 2-7. Fruit is large, oval, dark blue and very sweet, recommended for fresh eating and freezing. Ripens early to mid season; bloom time and mature size are not stated.

varieties.name: Honey Wild
varieties.summary: Easy-to-grow honeyberry sold by Berries Unlimited for fresh eating and cooking.
varieties.description: Sold by Berries Unlimited and described as a nice, easy-to-grow berry bush for fresh eating, freezing, cooking, baking and preserving. Rated for USDA zones 2-7. Bloom time, ripening and mature size are not stated.

varieties.name: Honey Gold
varieties.summary: Very late Japanese-origin honeyberry with large, round, sweet berries.
varieties.description: Listed by Berries Unlimited as a very late variety in its Blue Treasure family, of Japanese origin and a trademarked, patent-pending (PPAF) plant whose propagation is prohibited. Berries are large, round and sweet; the seller rates it for zones 2-7 with about 1,200 chilling hours and quotes yields of 6-12 lb per plant.

varieties.name: Wild Beast
varieties.summary: Honeyberry sold by Berries Unlimited for fresh eating and freezing.
varieties.description: Sold by Berries Unlimited for fresh eating and freezing and rated for USDA zones 2-7. Listed separately from Honey Beast on the seller's page. Origin, bloom time and mature size are not stated.

varieties.name: Blue Cloud
varieties.summary: Late-season Japanese-origin honeyberry listed by Berries Unlimited.
varieties.description: Listed by Berries Unlimited as a late variety of Japanese origin. Only the category-page listing was read, so fruit and plant details are not yet confirmed.

varieties.name: WildTreasure
varieties.summary: Early-mid season honeyberry sold by Berries Unlimited in gallon pots.
varieties.description: Listed by Berries Unlimited in its early-mid season group, rated for zones 2-7 and sold in a gallon size. The seller suggests uses including muffins, pies, jam, juice, wine and liquor.
